question: How many Florida counties will have reported locally acquired dengue cases in 2026, per the latest Florida Arbovirus Surveillance report available around September 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Prior from the 2024 analogue: the mid-September (Wk37) 2024 report listed locally acquired dengue from 7 counties, rising to 8 by Wk41 and 10 by year end - so 7 is the reference-class anchor for a mid-September report in an active transmission year. 2026 stands at 5 counties in the Wk34 report (73 cases, Hillsborough 59) with two more counties already announced by local DOH offices but not yet listed (Citrus Aug 26, Orange Sep 2), which is the key upward pipeline. Offsetting that, the state report's own county count has added only one county in three weeks (4/4/5 across Wk32-34) and demonstrably lags county announcements by over a week, so a Wk35-or-Wk36 report could plausibly still show only 6-7. Which report resolves is itself uncertain (Wk35 publishes ~Sep 10, Wk36 ~Sep 17-19 against a Sep 18 deadline). Count is cumulative and can essentially only rise from 5. No prediction market prices this. Escape above 13 would need +9 counties in under three weeks - no historical precedent even in 2023-24 - so priced at 1.5%.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the county count stated in the most recent weekly 'Florida Arbovirus Surveillance' PDF published by Florida DOH and available by 23:59 ET 2026-09-18 - NOT off county-level DOH press releases, news tallies, CDC data, or mosquito-pool positives. Travel-associated cases and positive mosquito pools do not add counties. Cumulative year-to-date by onset in calendar 2026.

EVENT WINDOW: 2026-01-01 -> 2026-09-18 per the criteria (onset in 2026; report available by the Sep 18 deadline); as of Now 2026-09-07T23:00Z, ~96% elapsed.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: the figure printed in the Week 34 report (5 counties: Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Pinellas, Palm Beach, Pasco) carried forward unchanged.

EVIDENCE:
- Week 34 report (data week Aug 23-29, 2026): 73 locally acquired dengue cases from 5 counties - Hillsborough 59, Miami-Dade 7, Pinellas 5, Palm Beach 1, Pasco 1. Confirmed by Fox 13 Tampa Bay, 2026-09-04, quoting '73 locally acquired dengue cases across Florida this year through Aug. 29'.
- Week 32 report (Aug 9-15, 2026): 23 cases from 4 counties (Hillsborough 15, Miami-Dade 4, Pinellas 3, Palm Beach 1), onset July (14) and August (9). Week 33 also listed 4 counties. Source: floridahealth.gov PDF fl-arbovirus-report-w32-2026.pdf.
- Report-internal county trajectory 2026: Wk32 = 4, Wk33 = 4, Wk34 = 5.
- DOH-Citrus announced a confirmed locally acquired dengue case on 2026-08-26 (WUFT, 2026-08-26 16:39 EDT; WFLA). Citrus does NOT appear in the Week 34 report published roughly a week later.
- DOH-Orange confirmed a locally acquired dengue case on 2026-09-02 (Orange County government newsroom release, Sept 2026; Fox 35 Orlando). Orange does NOT appear in the Week 34 report.
- Florida Surgeon General publicly described Hillsborough as the 'epicenter', citing ~59 cases and stating the number is expected to increase (WFLA, early Sept 2026). All Hillsborough cases typed DENV-2.
- Report publication cadence 2026: Wk32 and Wk33 PDFs sit in the /2026/08/ upload folder; the Wk34 PDF sits in /2026/09/ and was being cited by media on 2026-09-04 - implying roughly a 5-7 day lag from week end to publication. On that cadence Wk35 (ends Sep 5) publishes ~Sep 10-12 and Wk36 (ends Sep 12) ~Sep 17-19.

BASE RATES:
- Over Florida years with active local dengue transmission, as of the mid-September weekly report: 2024 Week 37 (Sep 8-14) listed 35 locally acquired cases from 7 counties (Hillsborough 3, Manatee 1, Miami-Dade 22, Monroe 3, Orange 2, Palm Beach 1, Pasco 3). Source: 2024-37-arbovirus-surveillance.pdf.
- Same class, later in the same season: 2024 Week 41 (Oct 6-12) = 47 cases from 8 counties; 2024 full year = 87 cases from 10 counties (Broward, Hillsborough, Manatee, Miami-Dade, Monroe, Orange, Palm Beach, Pasco, Polk, Sarasota). So +1 county over Wk37->Wk41 (4 weeks) and +3 over Wk37->year end (15 weeks).
- Conditional on a low-transmission year: 2025 full year = 4 counties (Brevard, Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Pasco).
- Conditional on the 2026 report itself (the instrument that resolves this): county additions have run at +1 per two weeks across Wk32-34, while local-DOH announcements of new counties have run at roughly one per week over the same stretch (Pasco, Citrus, Orange).

EVIDENCE FOR EXPANSION: case count tripled Wk32->Wk34 (23 -> 73); two counties publicly announced and not yet reflected in the report; transmission has moved north of Tampa Bay and into Central Florida per county announcements; September-November is the historical peak of Florida's Aedes transmission season; multiple counties under mosquito-borne illness alerts.
EVIDENCE FOR STASIS: the state report is the resolution instrument and adds counties more slowly than press releases; a county announced 2026-08-26 was still absent from a report published ~2026-09-02/04, so a >1-week classification lag is demonstrated, not hypothetical; 59 of 73 cases sit in one county, i.e. the outbreak is concentrated rather than broadly geographically seeded; 2024's analogous window added only ~1 county per month in the state report; the Wk36 report may not publish before the Sep 18 deadline, in which case the Wk35 data cut (onset through Sep 5) governs.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: the Week 35 or Week 36 2026 report (not yet published as of Now); machine-readable text of the Week 33/34 2026 PDFs (the files are image/compressed and did not extract, so their county sentences are known only via media quotation and the report index); a published DOH statement explaining why Citrus is absent from the Week 34 report (whether pending confirmation, exposure-county reassignment, or simple lag); the 2024 Week 34/35 reports, which would give a direct same-window county delta; any prediction market on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or a bookmaker covering Florida dengue county counts - none found on any venue checked.
calls.reference_class: Florida DOH weekly arbovirus surveillance reports in years with active local dengue transmission (2023-2025): the cumulative count of counties reporting locally acquired dengue as of the mid-September report, and the observed week-over-week rate at which counties are added during the August-October

calls.reasoning: Floor is hard: the tally is cumulative year-to-date, so it can only rise from the 5 counties in the Week 34 report (Hillsborough 59, Miami-Dade 7, Pinellas 5, Palm Beach 1, Pasco 1 = 73 cases). Reference class (peak-season 2-3 week increments in the state report's county count, 2024 and 2026 to date) implies a base rate of about +1 county, i.e. ~6. Two case-specific updates push above that: DOH-Orange confirmed a locally-acquired case on Sept 2 in its own press release, and DOH-Citrus announced one on Aug 26 - neither appears in the Week 34 report. Orange should enter the Week 35/36 report almost surely; Citrus is more doubtful since it was announced four days before the Week 34 data cutoff and still did not appear, which is consistent with pending classification review or reclassification as travel-associated. Counterargument for a lower number: 2026 transmission is unusually concentrated (81% of cases in Hillsborough alone) versus the geographically dispersed 2024 season, and the state report lags county announcements, so the narrow Sept 7-12 window leaves little room for further additions. Publication timing is the other uncertainty - if the resolving report is Week 35 rather than Week 36, one fewer week of data accrues.

Counting is cumulative year-to-date for 2026 onsets, so the figure is monotone non-decreasing across reports.

EVIDENCE BULLETS:

- DOH-Orange press release via Orange County newsroom, 2026-09-02: 'The Florida Department of Health in Orange County (DOH-Orange) confirmed a human case of locally-acquired dengue on September 2, 2026.' DOH-Orange had already issued a mosquito-borne illness advisory on 2026-08-27. Orange does NOT appear in the Week 34 report.
- Precedent on lag direction: DOH-Pasco issued an updated mosquito-borne illness advisory on 2026-08-26 and Pasco DID appear in the Week 34 report - i.e. one county announcing in that window entered the next report while another (Citrus) did not.

- Serotype/concentration note: all 59 Hillsborough cases and the single Pasco case are DENV-2; Hillsborough alone is 81% of the 73 statewide locally acquired cases - a single dominant cluster rather than dispersed statewide transmission.
- Travel-associated dengue is widespread and does NOT add counties: as of Aug 22 the report listed travel cases in Broward (12), Polk (2), Manatee (1), Osceola (1), Seminole (1) among others; 86 travel cases statewide as of Week 32.

BASE RATES (with the class each is computed over):
- Over full calendar year 2024 (all locally acquired dengue): 10 counties, ~91 cases - Broward (2), Hillsborough (7), Manatee (8), Miami-Dade (47), Monroe (3), Orange (2), Palm Beach (3), Pasco (13), Polk, Sarasota (1). Source: Florida DOH 2024 year-end arbovirus report.
- Over 2024 CONDITIONAL on the same calendar point (Week 37 report, Sep 8-14, 2024): 7 counties, 35 cases - Hillsborough (3), Manatee, Miami-Dade (22), Monroe (3), Orange (2), Palm Beach, Pasco (3). So in 2024, 3 of the year's 10 counties were added after mid-September.
- Over full calendar year 2025: 4 counties (Brevard, Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Pasco).
- Over 2026 to date, per-report increments in the county count during the active outbreak: W32 -> W33 = +0, W33 -> W34 = +1.
- Over the 2024 season, county-count trajectory across a comparable 2-3 week peak-season window: increments of roughly 0 to +3.

MARKET/CROWD: no prediction market found. Manifold API keyword search for Florida dengue returned an empty result set (checked 2026-09-07); the harness title search on Polymarket and Manifold also found no candidate; no Kalshi or bookmaker contract on Florida dengue county counts located.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: the Week 35 or Week 36 2026 report PDFs (not yet published; direct URL guess returned 404); the full text of the Week 34 PDF (PDF text extraction failed, so the county list is taken from the Fox 13 quotation of it rather than read directly); any Florida DOH statement on why the Citrus case is absent from the Week 34 report or on its final case classification; any documented Florida DOH publication schedule stating the exact posting day of week; any county first-local-case announcement dated Sept 3-7, 2026.

CAUTION ON SOURCES: several aggregator sites (medicaldaily.com, time.news, archyde.com, world-today-journal.com) recycle these stories with internally inconsistent figures (e.g. '41 locally transmitted infections' alongside '59 in Hillsborough'); the primary county DOH releases, the state report index, and the local broadcast outlets quoting the state report directly are the reliable layer.
calls.reference_class: Cumulative locally-acquired dengue county counts in successive Florida DOH weekly arbovirus surveillance reports during peak season (Aug-Nov), 2024 and 2026 year-to-date - specifically the number of new counties added over a 2-3 week data window

calls.reasoning: Prior from FDOH mid-September cumulative county counts in prior local-dengue seasons (2023 ~4, 2024 ~8, 2025 ~3; year-end 5/10/4) anchors near 5, and the count is monotone from the current 5 in the W34 report (73 cases: Hillsborough 59, Miami-Dade 7, Pinellas 5, Palm Beach 1, Pasco 1). Publication lag is ~4-7 days after week end, so the report available on Sep 18 is most likely W36 (onsets through Sep 12), with meaningful chance it is only W35 - i.e. one or two more report-weeks of accrual. Two counties are already in the announcement pipeline but absent from W34: Orange (confirmed Sep 2) and Citrus (announced ~Aug 22), the latter's two-report absence being real evidence that county announcements do not reliably convert into the state tally on schedule. Against that, the Hillsborough cluster added 32 cases in a single week and Tampa Bay spillover (Pasco, Pinellas already listed) plus Orlando and Miami-Dade activity make one or two further first-time counties plausible over the remaining weeks. Median 7; right skew to 10 at the 90th for a fast-expanding footprint or a backlog catch-up; 5 retained at ~12% for the case where nothing new is classified in time.

Only locally acquired (non-travel) human cases with 2026 onset; travel cases and positive mosquito pools do not add counties.

EVENT WINDOW: onset window is 2026-01-01 -> 2026-12-31 per the criteria, but the operative cutoff is the data cutoff of whichever weekly report is latest by the deadline. As of Now (2026-09-07T23:00Z), 68% of calendar 2026 has elapsed; the latest posted report (W34) covers onsets through 2026-08-29, i.e. 66% of the calendar year.

Source: FDOH weekly arbovirus report series.

calls.reference_class: Florida DOH weekly Arbovirus Surveillance reports during active local-dengue seasons (2023, 2024, 2025): the cumulative count of counties with locally acquired dengue as of the mid-September report, and the observed week-over-week growth in that count during the Aug-Oct peak.

calls.reasoning: The tally is cumulative and monotone from the 5 counties in the W34 report (73 cases, Hillsborough 59). The instrument itself has added just one county in three cycles (4/4/5) while three counties announced, so the base rate for 1-2 more report-weeks is about +1, i.e. 6. Two case-specific updates lift that: Orange has a DOH-confirmed locally acquired case (Sep 2) with onset inside the W35 window that should enter retroactively, and Citrus (announced Aug 26, not Aug 22) has missed only one post-announcement cutoff - ordinary lag, not evidence of non-conversion. Against: 81% of cases sit in one county, so this is a concentrated cluster rather than dispersed seeding, and 2023 showed 154+ cases confined to five counties all year. I decline Run 1's anchoring on 2024's mid-September level of 7, since 2024 was already geographically dispersed by August. Labor Day (Sep 7, 2026), which no run noted, adds slip risk to whether W36 clears the Sep 18 deadline, so I hold the resolver at only ~55-60% W36. Median 7, floor 5 at ~13%, right tail to 9-10 for a backlog catch-up.
calls.reconciliation: Three disputes were factual and two of them settled cleanly on the dossiers. (a) Citrus's announcement date is Aug 26, not ~Aug 22 - Run 3's own dossier cites WUFT 2026-08-26 while its reasoning says Aug 22. That matters directionally: Citrus has been absent from exactly one report whose cutoff (Aug 29) postdates the announcement, so Run 3's 'announced counties fail to convert' inference is weaker than it claimed, and Citrus's conversion odds go up to about 0.5. (b) The 2024 Week 37 count is 7, not ~8, on an explicit named county list from the 2024 PDF cited by two runs. (c) Which report resolves could NOT be settled - no run found a published FDOH posting schedule and W35 was unpublished at Now. I add one fact all three missed: Labor Day fell on Monday Sep 7, 2026, which can push W35 to ~Sep 11-12 and W36 to ~Sep 17-18, right against the deadline; I therefore hold W36 at only ~55-60% rather than treating it as the default, and that uncertainty is carried in the low tail rather than resolved by fiat. On judgment, I rejected Run 1's anchoring on 2024's mid-September LEVEL of 7 - 2024 was geographically dispersed by August whereas 2026 is 81% one county, so the transferable statistic is the county-ADDITION rate, not the level - and I rejected Run 2's 2.6-count width as too tight given the unresolved resolver question and backlog-dump risk. I carry Run 3's reference class (peak-season 2-3 week increments in the report's own county count) forward, agreeing with it, but combine it with the pipeline explicitly: Orange ~0.85, Citrus ~0.5, one genuinely new county ~0.6-0.8, giving ~2 expected additions off a hard floor of 5. Median 6.9 with 5 held at ~13%. Landing near Runs 2 and 3 is coincidental in route, not a compromise: I moved Run 3's Citrus estimate up and Run 1's anchor down, and the corrections happened to meet near 7. Escape above 13.5 would require nine new counties in under three weeks, with no precedent in 2023 or 2024, so it is priced at 0.5%. I retrieved nothing myself on this run - no web access - so sources is empty.

disagreements.verdict: Rejected. It prices Orange-plus-maybe-Citrus and nothing else, while ignoring resolver uncertainty and the possibility of a backlog addition in a season that added 32 cases in the W34 week alone. Width set at ~4.1, near Runs 1 and 3.
